eras.label: 3000–1 BCE · Regional cultures and oral traditions
1–1499 CE · Religious traditions and historical sources

events.title: Palaeolithic traditions
events.summary: Broad chapter convention; newer site chronologies extend beyond this band. Hunting–gathering, flaked tools, caves and open sites; regional transitions overlap.

events.title: Upper Palaeolithic reference horizon
events.summary: Blades, burins, bone tools, ornaments and painting; not the first appearance of Homo sapiens.

events.title: Mesolithic traditions
events.summary: Microlithic tools, hunting/fishing/gathering, rock art and changing settlement patterns; later survival and herding vary by region.

events.title: Beginning of the Holocene
events.summary: Approximate BCE placement of the geological boundary. Later forager and early farming cultures overlap this epoch; cultural boundaries are regional.

events.date_label: Conventionally c.7000 BCE; revised dating disputed
events.title: Early farming at Mehrgarh
events.summary: Conventional textbook placement before urban Harappa. A 2025 tooth-enamel study instead places Period I about 5250–4650 cal BCE; retain the distinction rather than two supposedly separate settlements.

events.title: Regional Neolithic cultures
events.summary: Farming/herding, ground tools, durable villages and pottery in many phases. Conventional earlier Mehrgarh dates lie outside this simplified band.

events.title: Early Harappan / Regionalisation
events.summary: Regional villages and fortified towns, crafts, trade and wheeled transport develop; dates vary by site.

events.title: Burzahom habitation sequence
events.summary: Kashmir site spans Neolithic, Megalithic and early historical phases; pit dwellings and human/animal burials are important. This is not one homogeneous 2000-year Neolithic phase.

events.title: Chalcolithic regional cultures
events.summary: Copper and stone, rural production/crafts/exchange. Some phases precede or overlap Harappa; others follow it.

events.title: Ahar–Banas reference band
events.summary: Banas basin; Ahar, Gilund and Balathal; chapter chronology, with broader regional ranges in other studies.

events.title: Mature Harappan / Integration
events.summary: Large cities, shared script/seals, weights and brick proportions; regional diversity persists.

events.title: Northeastern Neolithic reference horizon
events.summary: Broad chapter range, or later; Daojali Hading and Garo hills illustrate regional diversity.

events.title: Kayatha reference band
events.summary: Chhoti Kali Sindh/Chambal drainage, Madhya Pradesh; dates depend on phase and excavation.

events.title: Indo-Aryan movements and interactions
events.summary: Broad second-millennium BCE context for movements through Central Asia and interaction in South Asia. Linguistic, archaeological and genetic evidence have different scopes; neither pottery nor DNA directly identifies an individual’s language.

events.title: Late Harappan / Localisation
events.summary: Urban contraction, regional settlement/craft changes and agricultural adaptation; not complete disappearance of population or culture.

events.title: Prabhas reference band
events.summary: Prabhas Patan/Somnath, Gujarat; chapter reference chronology.

events.title: Malwa reference band
events.summary: Navdatoli on the Narmada; regional Chalcolithic culture.

events.title: Early / Rig Vedic phase
events.summary: Northwestern geographical emphasis; pastoralism alongside cultivation; jana, chiefs and assemblies; older Rigvedic family books. Boundaries are conventional and approximate.

events.title: Vedic textual composition traditions
events.summary: Broad conventional range for Vedic oral/textual traditions; early Rigvedic and later Vedic layers overlap regional cultural changes. Oral composition, textual layering and surviving manuscript dates are distinct.

events.title: Jorwe reference band
events.summary: Maharashtra; Jorwe, Inamgaon, Daimabad and Chandoli. Sites occupy different tributaries and phases.

events.title: Later Vedic phase
events.summary: Kuru–Panchala and eastward expansion; agriculture, stronger territorial kingship, elaborate sacrifice and philosophical inquiry. Some periodisations end this phase around 600 BCE.

events.title: Dharmasutra traditions
events.summary: Broad chapter composition band for normative texts on conduct and social duties; dates differ by text. Prescriptions must not be equated with universal practice.

events.title: Second urbanisation and territorial states
events.summary: Ganga-basin towns, surplus agriculture, craft specialisation, trade, early coinage and larger territorial states; regional chronologies vary. Agrarian surplus, crafts, coins, trade and new social groups formed the setting for Buddhist, Jaina and other shramana movements. Economic change is one factor, not a complete explanation of every doctrine.

events.title: Upanishadic inquiry in the later Vedic setting
events.summary: Around this broad horizon, traditions associated with Panchala and Videha develop discussions of self, knowledge, action and liberation. This does not date every Upanishad to one year; early texts and later layers span a wider period.

events.title: Mahavira: traditional life chronology
events.summary: Traditional dates used in the chapter; historical chronologies vary. Twenty-fourth Tirthankara; Kundagrama near Vaishali, Jnatrika clan; final liberation associated with Pavapuri. Ages and family details belong to traditions with sect differences.

events.title: Gautama Buddha: conventional life chronology
events.summary: One traditional chronology, not an uncontested historical dating. Lumbini birth; renunciation, enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, first sermon at Sarnath, final passing at Kushinara. Some historical chronologies place his life later.

events.title: Cyrus and the eastern Achaemenid frontier
events.summary: Expansion towards northwestern South Asia belongs to the sixth-century BCE background; exact local Indian conquest claims remain uncertain.

events.title: Bimbisara consolidates Magadha
events.summary: Haryanka ruler; Rajagriha capital, conquest of Anga, matrimonial alliances and diplomacy. Founder status and precise regnal dates are not certain.

events.title: Darius I extends authority in the Indus region
events.summary: Persian incorporation/consolidation in parts of the northwest; Gandara and Hindush are separate imperial geographical names, not all India.

events.title: Indian and Gandarian troops in Persian service
events.summary: Contingents appear in accounts of Xerxes' campaigns against Greece; does not imply Persian conquest of the whole subcontinent.

events.title: Ajatashatru expands Magadha
events.summary: Conflict over Kashi and defeat of Vajji; war-machine traditions and Vassakara diplomacy. Buddhist tradition places Buddha's death and First Council in his reign, but absolute chronologies differ.

events.date_label: c.483 BCE · traditional date; chronology disputed
events.title: First Buddhist council: Rajagriha tradition
events.summary: Traditionally shortly after Buddha’s passing, under Ajatashatru, led by Mahakassapa; Upali recites discipline and Ananda discourses. Absolute date follows one Buddha chronology; do not imply the entire later Abhidhamma was already fixed.

events.title: Udayin and the capital at Pataliputra
events.summary: Associated with transferring the Magadhan capital to Pataliputra at strategic ancient river junctions; not Udayana of Vatsa.

events.title: Shishunaga dynasty
events.summary: Shishunaga annexes Avanti and is associated with Vaishali; Kalashoka with Pataliputra and the Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali. Exact chronology varies.

events.date_label: c.fourth–third centuries BCE · later traditional association
events.title: Bhadrabahu and southward migration: traditional setting
events.summary: Later traditions connect a twelve-year Magadhan famine, Bhadrabahu’s movement south and Chandragupta Maurya’s Jaina renunciation at Shravanabelagola. Not an independently established exact itinerary or a single instantaneous sectarian split.

events.title: Jaina Pataliputra council and transmission traditions
events.summary: Associated with Sthulabhadra and recovering/arranging Angas. Source’s 310 BCE is a teaching convention, not an established exact date. Related famine/migration accounts are later traditions; Digambara tradition does not accept this recension as authoritative.

events.title: Mahabharata: layered composition
events.summary: Broad conventional composition/redaction band, with oral formation and later layers. The epic’s story setting is not the date of its surviving textual compilation.

events.title: Ramayana: layered composition
events.summary: Broad chapter composition band; the received text contains different layers. Traditional story chronology is distinct from historical composition dates.

events.date_label: c.383 BCE · conventional date; chronology disputed
events.title: Second Buddhist council: Vaishali tradition
events.summary: Traditionally about a century after Buddha, associated with Kalashoka and Sabbakami; discipline disputes. Accounts of the early Sthavira–Mahasanghika division vary.

events.title: Life of Alexander III of Macedon
events.summary: Son of Philip II; died at Babylon in 323 BCE, not in his Punjab campaign year 326 BCE.

events.title: Nanda expansion
events.summary: Mahapadma Nanda associated with wider conquest, including Kalinga, taxation and irrigation; Dhana Nanda is the last major ruler. Origin and army-size traditions require caution.

events.title: Alexander campaigns in northwestern South Asia
events.summary: Campaign through the northwest and Punjab, return down the Indus and land/sea withdrawal. Resistance extended beyond Porus; no Magadha conquest.

events.date_label: 326 BCE · no exact within-year sequence implied
events.title: Army refuses advance beyond the Hyphasis / Beas
events.summary: Beas becomes the eastern limit; no march to the Ganga or battle against the Nandas.

events.title: Battle of the Hydaspes / Jhelum
events.summary: Alexander defeats Porus and restores him as a subordinate ruler; Porus was not Ambhi of Taxila.

events.title: Alexander dies at Babylon
events.summary: His death is followed by successor struggles; Seleucus was not immediately appointed ruler of all northwestern India during the Indian retreat.

events.title: Chandragupta Maurya’s reign
events.summary: Approximate conventional dates; Nanda overthrow, north-western consolidation, Seleucus agreement and Pataliputra court.

events.title: Chandragupta establishes Mauryan rule
events.summary: Overthrow of the Nandas, traditionally with Kautilya's assistance; slightly different accession dates occur in scholarship.

events.title: Mauryan imperial period
events.summary: Common approximate reconstruction; chapter uses c.324–187 BCE. Political control varied by region.

events.title: Chandragupta–Seleucus conflict and settlement
events.summary: Territorial and diplomatic settlement; 500 elephants for Seleucus; exact marriage and boundary details debated.

events.title: Megasthenes at the Mauryan court
events.summary: Broad conventional setting after Seleucus settlement; Indica survives in later authors, not the original.

events.date_label: c.third century BCE–third century CE · broad building range
events.title: Amaravati stupa develops through multiple phases
events.summary: Dhanyakataka/Amaravati in Andhra Pradesh was an important Buddhist centre with Mahasanghika associations. Stupa construction and alteration extended over centuries; not one uniformly dated building.

events.title: Ashokan inscriptions and artistic connections
events.summary: Northwestern Kharoshthi inscriptions and possible Persian connections in Mauryan royal display; bell-shaped capitals belong to pillars, not rock edicts.

events.title: Buddhist mission traditions under Ashoka
events.summary: Sri Lankan chronicles associate Mahinda and Sanghamitta with Sri Lanka; Sona/Uttara with Suvarnabhumi, Mahadeva with Mahishamandala, Majjhima with Himalayan region, Dhammarakkhita with Aparantaka and Maharakkhita with Yona country. Exact destination boundaries are debated.

events.title: Mauryan cave patronage for Ajivikas
events.summary: Third-century BCE inscriptions at Barabar and Nagarjuni, associated with Ashoka and Dasharatha, provide important evidence for Ajivika patronage beyond rival textual accounts.

events.title: Sanchi: Ashokan brick nucleus
events.summary: The Great Stupa began with an Ashokan-period brick nucleus; later enlargements, stone casing and gateways belong to further building phases.

events.title: Sangam literary reference period
events.summary: Broad conventional span; Silappadikaram and Manimekalai are later/post-Sangam epics, not evidence for a single composition date.

events.title: Bindusara’s reign
events.summary: Approximate conventional chronology; Amitrochates/Amitraghata, southern consolidation and diplomatic contacts.

events.title: Ashoka’s accession and consecration traditions
events.summary: Alternative chronologies distinguish accession c.273 and later consecration c.268; succession stories are literary traditions.

events.title: Ashoka’s consecrated reign
events.summary: Conventional chronology used for regnal-year reference; dates remain approximate.

events.title: Kalinga war
events.summary: Conventional c.261 BCE; eighth year after consecration; Major Rock Edict XIII records suffering and remorse.

events.title: Ashoka’s Sambodhi visit and dhamma tours
events.summary: Approximate placement from ten years after consecration; Major Rock Edict VIII.

events.title: Touring instructions and royal moral communications
events.summary: Twelve years after consecration in edict evidence; yuktas, rajukas and pradesikas to inspect every five years. Absolute year approximate.

events.title: Dhamma-mahamatras appointed
events.summary: Thirteen years after consecration in Major Rock Edict V; absolute year approximate.

events.title: Konakamana stupa enlarged
events.summary: Nigali Sagar inscription places enlargement in 14th year; c.254 BCE approximate.

events.title: Third Buddhist council: Pataliputra tradition
events.summary: Theravada accounts associate Ashoka and Moggaliputta Tissa with doctrinal purification, Kathavatthu and missions. Not all school histories narrate the same council.

events.title: Ashoka visits Lumbini and Nigali Sagar
events.summary: Twentieth-year records; Lumbini bali exemption and produce share reduced to one-eighth. Absolute year approximate.

events.title: Late major pillar edicts
events.summary: Twenty-sixth and twenty-seventh years after consecration; approximate placement. Judicial fairness, protection and policy retrospective.

events.title: Ashoka dies
events.summary: Approximate conventional date; subsequent regional fragmentation and succession problems.

events.title: Dasharatha’s conventional reign
events.summary: Later Maurya associated with Nagarjuni cave dedications to Ajivikas; approximate reign dates.

events.title: Antiochus III’s north-western expedition
events.summary: Distinct from Alexander’s earlier campaign and from subsequent Indo-Greek expansion; not the first Greek arrival in India.

events.date_label: second century BCE · principal surviving sculpture
events.title: Bharhut: railings, sculpture and donors
events.summary: Famous surviving railings and narrative sculpture are largely second-century BCE. Inscriptions record lay, monastic and female donors; earlier Ashokan foundation is conventionally attributed, not a uniform date for every element.

events.title: Dharmashastra / Smriti development
events.summary: Broad chapter band for a diverse normative literary tradition; not the date of one single text or a universally enforced legal code.

events.date_label: c.second–first centuries BCE · broad reference period
events.title: Jaina associations in the Tamil south
events.summary: The last centuries BCE form an early southern reference horizon for Jaina communities and Tamil-Brahmi associations; regional transmission and dating are not one single event.

events.title: Brihadratha killed; Shunga rule begins
events.summary: Pushyamitra’s takeover conventionally c.185 BCE; chapter gives c.187. Do not record both as separate events.

events.title: Kharavela and Jaina patronage in Kalinga
events.summary: Conventionally dated to the first century BCE; important Jaina royal patron. Do not place Kharavela in the fourth century BCE.

events.title: Pali canon writing: Sri Lankan fourth-council tradition
events.summary: Alu Vihara/Aloka Lena under Vattagamani Abhaya is associated with writing down the Pali canon. Separate from the later Kashmir council in Sarvastivada tradition.

events.title: Ashvaghosha and the Buddhacharita
events.summary: Sanskrit sacred life of Buddha; poet and dramatist traditionally linked with Kanishka. Broad first–second-century CE association.

events.title: Digambara and Shvetambara identities crystallise
events.summary: Differences in clothing, scripture, religious biography and women’s final liberation developed over centuries. Do not date a single fully formed split to one famine or one exact year.

events.date_label: first century CE · traditional mission account
events.title: Early Chinese invitation tradition
events.summary: Traditions associate Kashyapa Matanga and Dharmaratna with an early Chinese invitation and translation activity. This is a traditional account, not a verified itinerary for every similarly named monk.

events.title: Periplus of the Erythraean Sea
events.summary: Anonymous Greek-language account of navigation, ports and commodities; useful for Indian Ocean trade.

events.date_label: second century CE · broad Kanishka-period setting
events.title: Kashmir council under Kanishka
events.summary: Sarvastivada fourth-council tradition associated with Kashmir/Kundalavana, Vasumitra and scholastic commentaries. Not the instantaneous origin of Mahayana or a simple Mahayana/Hinayana division.

events.title: Nagarjuna and Madhyamaka
events.summary: Broad second–third-century CE placement. Madhyamaka and emptiness; Satavahana patronage traditions exist but identification of one exact contemporary king is debated.

events.title: Ptolemy’s Geography
events.summary: Greek geographical account supplying evidence on places, ports and trade.

events.title: Kanishka: modern accession framework
events.summary: The c.127 CE accession framework places Kanishka in the second century CE, explaining why older first-century datings of his council require qualification.

events.title: Rudradaman’s Junagadh inscription
events.summary: c.150 CE; records earlier Sudarshana lake construction under Pushyagupta and works under Tushaspha. Later evidence about Mauryan activity.

events.title: Asanga and Vasubandhu
events.summary: Brothers associated with Yogachara/Vijnanavada development; Vasubandhu’s Abhidharmakosha is a major Abhidharma work. Broad scholarly chronology, not exact life dates.

events.date_label: c.4th–6th centuries CE · major formation, not final closure
events.title: Major Puranic textual formation
events.summary: The chapter places important Puranic textual formation in the fourth–sixth centuries CE. These are layered traditions with earlier material and continuing later redaction, not uniformly completed books.

events.title: Faxian’s Indian journey
events.summary: Chinese Buddhist pilgrim; account illuminates Gupta-era society. The chapter’s 500 CE should not be treated as an exact visit date. Chinese pilgrim collected Buddhist texts and observed religious institutions; one of the translation/travel networks linking India and East Asia.

events.title: Buddhaghosa and the Visuddhimagga
events.summary: Fifth-century Pali scholar associated with the Path of Purification, a major Theravada synthesis.

events.title: Dhamekh: major surviving structural phase
events.summary: The present massive Dhamekh stupa at Sarnath is substantially Gupta-period, broadly fifth–sixth centuries CE, in a sacred landscape with earlier Ashokan remains. Avoid an unsupported exact reconstruction year.

events.title: Dignaga develops Buddhist logic
events.summary: Broad fifth–sixth-century CE setting; Buddhist logician and epistemologist, not Jaina.

events.title: Kumarajiva arrives at Chang’an
events.summary: An important stage in his Chinese Buddhist translation activity; do not describe every later translator of a similar name as the same individual.

events.date_label: fifth–sixth centuries CE · varying traditional dates
events.title: Vallabhi council and Shvetambara canonical redaction
events.summary: Associated with Devarddhigani Kshamashramana. Dates vary: 453/466 CE occur in scholarship; 512 CE in conventional teaching accounts. Surviving Shvetambara collection has eleven Angas, the twelfth lost; Digambaras preserve a different authoritative corpus.

events.title: Tamil devotional traditions expand
events.summary: Alvar and Nayanar hymns, temple networks and vernacular devotion developed under several dynasties; chronology varied regionally.

events.title: Dharmakirti and Buddhist epistemology
events.summary: Seventh-century Buddhist philosopher of logic and knowledge; distinguish him from similarly named translators.

events.date_label: from seventh century CE · growing popularity
events.title: Miniature votive stupas become especially common
events.summary: Seventh-century CE reference horizon for popular miniature terracotta offerings in India; votive objects also occur in stone and metal, and the practice is not limited to one century.

events.date_label: later first millennium CE · broad development horizon
events.title: Vajrayana develops in later first-millennium India
events.summary: Esoteric methods within a Mahayana framework: guru, initiation, mantra, mandala and visualisation. Especially important in eastern India; not reducible to magic or a single foundation year.

events.title: Xuanzang’s Indian journey
events.summary: Chinese Buddhist pilgrim associated with Harsha and Nalanda; 7th century, not an exact 700 CE visit. Chinese pilgrim and scholar; his travel/textual transmission contributed to connections between Indian Buddhist institutions and East Asia.

events.title: Early Sufi ascetic and devotional traditions
events.summary: Rabia, Bayazid Bistami and Junayd exemplify diverse early mystical traditions; substantial literature and institutions followed.

events.title: Eighth-century Buddhist transmission to Tibet
events.summary: An important early transmission phase; renewed eleventh-century links followed later. Neither date is the first existence of all Vajrayana ideas.

events.title: Jaina Harivamsha Purana
events.summary: Eighth-century Jaina epic-lineage work associated with Krishna, Balarama and other figures; distinguish similarly titled non-Jaina works.

events.title: Shankara: conventional life dates
events.summary: Advaita, liberating knowledge, major commentaries and the traditional four-matha association; precise chronology and some attributions are debated.

events.title: Jinasena, Gunabhadra and Jaina Puranic literature
events.summary: Ninth-century Adi Purana/Rishabha narrative and Trishashtilakshana Mahapurana tradition; sacred biography includes social and political material.

events.title: Alvar hymns assembled into the Divya Prabandham
events.summary: The anthology of approximately four thousand Tamil hymns acquired the standing of the Tamil Veda.

events.title: Hujwiri and Kashf al-Mahjub
events.summary: Lahore-based Sufi associated with a major Persian treatise on spiritual life.

events.date_label: eleventh century CE · renewed transmission phase
events.title: Renewed Buddhist transmissions to Tibet
events.summary: Eleventh-century renewed links with Indian teachers and institutions, including Vikramashila, were important to Tibetan lineages.

events.title: Ramanuja: traditional life dates
events.summary: Vishishtadvaita, real dependent souls/matter, personal Narayana, devotion, grace and surrender.

events.title: Akka Mahadevi’s devotional poetry
events.summary: Karnataka vachanas address Shiva as Chennamallikarjuna and challenge prescribed social conventions.

events.title: Basavanna and the Karnataka Sharana movement
events.summary: Kannada vachanas, spiritual experience, dignity of work and criticism of caste/gender exclusion; Anubhava Mantapa remembered as a discussion forum.

events.title: Hemachandra’s Parishishtaparvan
events.summary: Twelfth-century Jaina work on teachers and political traditions; a Jaina text unlike Buddhist Nettipakarana or Avadanashataka.

events.title: Jayadeva and Gita Govinda
events.summary: Radha–Krishna love expressed in a major devotional poem, influential in eastern Vaishnava traditions.

events.title: Kalhana’s Rajatarangini
events.summary: Kashmir historical narrative; evaluate literary form and retrospective traditions.

events.title: Northern devotional movements gain momentum
events.summary: Diverse Rama, Krishna and formless-devotion currents grew through regional language, performance, social criticism and institutions.

events.title: Bijjala’s rule: context for Basavanna
events.summary: Kalachuri ruler associated with Basavanna’s ministerial service.

events.date_label: late twelfth–early thirteenth centuries CE · approximate horizon
events.title: Attacks intensify losses of major Buddhist monasteries
events.summary: Late twelfth–early thirteenth-century warfare and attacks on institutions in parts of northern/eastern India intensified an already uneven decline. Not a universal extinction date or sole cause.

events.title: Baba Farid: conventional life dates
events.summary: Fariduddin Ganj-i Shakar; Chishti spiritual discipline and verses later included in Guru Granth Sahib.

events.title: Janabai’s devotional milieu
events.summary: Marathi poems connected household labour, devotion and experiences of caste/gender exclusion.

events.title: Urban and artisanal growth in explanations of Bhakti
events.summary: Expansion of craft production and towns is one interpretation of wider audiences and demands for dignity, rather than a universal single cause.

events.title: Death of Muinuddin Chishti
events.summary: Ajmer’s Gharib Nawaz became the centre of an enduring shrine tradition; Chishti name derives from Chisht, Afghanistan.

events.title: Madhva: traditional life dates
events.summary: Dvaita distinguishes Vishnu, souls and matter while affirming dependence on God; alternative chronologies exist.

events.title: Nizamuddin Auliya’s lifetime
events.summary: Delhi Chishti master: love, hospitality and distance from courtly dependence; associated with Khusrau and Hasan Sijzi.

events.title: Namdev: conventional life dates
events.summary: Vitthala devotion, Marathi abhangs and hymns preserved in Guru Granth Sahib.

events.title: Jnaneshwar’s lifetime
events.summary: Marathi Jnaneshwari, Amritanubhava and Haripath traditions helped widen devotional expression.

events.title: Burhanuddin Gharib and Deccan Chishtis
events.summary: Expansion into the Deccan; the source’s thirteenth-century placement is not adopted.

events.date_label: fourteenth century CE · debated late references
events.title: Late medieval references associated with Ajivikas
events.summary: Southern references are sometimes cited into the fourteenth century; identification and continuity with the ancient movement are debated. Not proof of a fully documented unbroken organisation.

events.title: Ramananda’s broad historical setting
events.summary: North Indian Rama–Sita devotion, vernacular teaching and Ramanandi traditions; exact life dates/disciple lists uncertain.

events.title: Vidyapati: conventional life dates
events.summary: Maithili poet of Shiva devotion and Radha–Krishna love.

events.title: Timur invades north India
events.summary: Crossing of Indus and invasion postdated Muhammad bin Tughluq; relevant to the ruler–event PYQ trap.

events.title: Kabir’s devotional setting
events.summary: Nirguna devotion, critique of empty ritual/caste and multiple verse traditions including Bijak; calendar placement is intentionally broad.

events.title: Mirabai’s devotional setting
events.summary: Krishna bhajans, Mewar/Rajput context and spiritual agency; biographical details mediated by later traditions.

events.title: Ravidas and devotional dignity
events.summary: Leather-working association, critique of caste exclusion and hymns preserved in Guru Granth Sahib.

events.title: Surdas in Braj devotional literature
events.summary: Sursagar, Sursaravali and Sahitya Lahari; Krishna devotion associated with the Vallabha tradition.

events.title: Annamacharya’s lifetime
events.summary: Telugu sankirtanas devoted to Venkateshwara; not a contemporary of Tyagaraja.

events.title: Narsinh Mehta: conventional life dates
events.summary: Gujarati Radha–Krishna devotion; Vaishnava Jan To remembered for compassion.

events.title: Shankaradeva’s lifetime
events.summary: Assamese devotional poetry/drama, Ekasarana tradition and satra/namghar networks.

events.title: Guru Nanak’s lifetime
events.summary: Founder of Sikhism; Naam, honest livelihood, sharing, service and community; Talwandi birthplace distinct from Kartarpur on Ravi.

events.title: Vallabhacharya’s lifetime
events.summary: Shuddhadvaita and Pushtimarg; Krishna/Shrinathji seva and grace.

events.title: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu’s lifetime
events.summary: Krishna devotion, sankirtan and Bengal–Odisha–Vrindavan networks.

events.title: Dias expedition rounds the Cape
events.summary: Voyage began in 1487; rounded southern Africa in 1488, opening the route later used to reach India.

events.title: Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut
events.summary: May arrival on the Kerala coast under the Zamorin; early modern Portuguese ocean route, not the first Europe–India contact.

events.title: Baqi Billah introduces Naqshbandi order in India
events.summary: Distinguish Indian introduction from the earlier Central Asian Bahauddin Naqshband lineage.

events.title: Hit Harivansh and Radha-Vallabha tradition
events.summary: Vernacular Radha devotion; the source’s unsupported precise 1585 founding date is excluded.

events.title: Tulsidas and Rama devotion
events.summary: Awadhi Ramcharitmanas gave Rama devotion enduring literary and performative forms.

events.title: Portuguese fort at Cochin
events.summary: Early fortified base supporting Indian Ocean trade.

events.title: Almeida's viceroyalty
events.summary: First Portuguese viceroy; naval supremacy associated with Blue Water Policy.

events.title: Albuquerque's governorship
events.summary: Consolidation through territorial bases and maritime choke points.

events.title: Portuguese conquest of Goa
events.summary: Albuquerque captured Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate.

events.title: Portuguese capture Malacca
events.summary: Albuquerque extended control over a strategic Southeast Asian trade route.

events.title: Portuguese occupation of Hormuz
events.summary: Albuquerque established a base at the Persian Gulf entrance.

events.title: Babur’s victory ends the Lodi dynasty
events.summary: Chronological background to the saint-contemporaneity question: Nanak was alive, while Dadu and Tyagaraja belonged to later generations.

events.title: Portuguese headquarters move to Goa
events.summary: Nuno da Cunha shifted headquarters from Cochin; distinct from the 1510 conquest.

events.title: Eknath’s lifetime
events.summary: Marathi religious literature, bharuds, Bhavarth Ramayan and a recension of Jnaneshwari.

events.title: Bassein ceded to Portuguese
events.summary: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat ceded Bassein and dependencies.

events.title: Diu fortification agreement
events.summary: Gujarat permitted Portuguese fortification under pressure from Mughal expansion.

events.title: Guruship of Guru Angad
events.summary: Gurmukhi standardisation/popularisation, education, langar and physical training.

events.title: Dadu Dayal’s lifetime
events.summary: Non-sectarian Nirguna devotion, Rajasthan activity and Dadu Panth; Kabir was earlier, not his disciple.

events.title: Guruship of Guru Amar Das
events.summary: Manji organisation, langar, women preachers and opposition to discriminatory social practices.

events.title: Printing press arrives in Goa
events.summary: Early printing associated with Portuguese missionary activity.

events.title: Portuguese acquire Daman
events.summary: Expansion of northern Portuguese coastal possessions.

events.title: Garcia da Orta's medicinal-plant work
events.summary: Coloquios contributed to European knowledge of Asian plants; Indian medical traditions already existed.

events.title: Ahmad Sirhindi’s lifetime
events.summary: Naqshbandi thinker stressing sharia and criticising some Akbar-era policies; not Kabir’s teacher.

events.title: Battle of Talikota
events.summary: Vijayanagara's defeat accelerated regional realignments; Mysore's Wodeyar dynasty already existed.

events.title: Guruship of Guru Ram Das
events.summary: Development of Ramdaspur/Amritsar and Lavan hymns.

events.title: Amritsar/Ramdaspur develops
events.summary: Town and tank associated with Guru Ram Das; later shrine construction and Granth installation are distinct events.

events.title: Guruship of Guru Arjan
events.summary: Harmandir and community centres, compilation of Adi Granth; executed under Jahangir.

events.title: Houtman reaches Java
events.summary: Dutch voyage to Banten, not a landing in India.

events.title: English East India Company charter
events.summary: Elizabeth I granted a 15-year monopoly on 31 December.

events.title: Bahinabai’s devotional poetry
events.summary: Marathi abhangs explore spiritual and household tensions; distinguish the later modern poet of the same name.

events.title: Dutch VOC established
events.summary: Joint-stock company combined trading capital with treaty, fortification and war powers.

events.title: Adi Granth installed at Harmandir Sahib
events.summary: Guru Arjan’s compilation included Gurus’ hymns and devotional voices from diverse traditions.

events.title: Dutch factory at Masulipatnam
events.summary: Earliest Dutch factory in India; distinguish Pulicat among the 2003 PYQ's choices.

events.title: Akal Takht established
events.summary: Guru Hargobind associated temporal authority with spiritual responsibility.

events.title: Guru Arjan executed under Jahangir
events.summary: Major watershed in Sikh–Mughal relations; religious and political tensions form the context.

events.title: Guruship of Guru Hargobind
events.summary: Miri–Piri, two swords, armed defence and community institutions.

events.title: Hawkins arrives at Surat
events.summary: Arrival on Hector preceded his court mission.

events.title: Samarth Ramdas’s lifetime
events.summary: Rama devotion, Dasbodh, Manache Shlok and disciplined action; precise Shivaji-guru narratives debated.

events.title: Tukaram’s lifetime
events.summary: Marathi abhangs, Vitthala devotion, compassion and criticism of hypocrisy.

events.title: English trading charter renewed
events.summary: James I renewed the Company's monopoly arrangement.

events.title: Hawkins visits Jahangir
events.summary: Trading negotiations met Portuguese opposition.

events.title: Dutch establish Pulicat base
events.summary: Important Coromandel settlement and later Fort Geldria headquarters.

events.title: English factory at Masulipatnam
events.summary: First English factory in South India.

events.title: Battle of Swally
events.summary: Thomas Best's naval victory over Portuguese forces near Surat.

events.title: English Surat factory permitted
events.summary: Jahangir's reign; followed the Swally victory.

events.title: Thomas Roe's embassy
events.summary: James I's ambassador negotiated with Jahangir for commercial protection.

events.title: Danish company established
events.summary: Company formation preceded Tranquebar settlement.

events.title: Batavia founded
events.summary: Dutch base on Java; not conquest of the whole island.

events.title: Danish settlement at Tranquebar
events.summary: Tharangambadi became the Danish southern Indian base.

events.title: Amboyna incident
events.summary: Executions sharpened Anglo-Dutch commercial rivalry.

events.title: Golconda's Golden Farman
events.summary: Trading privilege for English Company commerce.

events.title: Mughal capture of Hooghly
events.summary: Shah Jahan's forces took the Portuguese settlement.

events.title: English factories in Odisha
events.summary: Hariharpur and Balasore were early English footholds in Eastern India.

events.title: Madras land grant
events.summary: Day and Cogan obtained land from Venkatadri Nayak under Vijayanagara/Chandragiri authority.

events.title: Fort St George built
events.summary: First English fort in India, at Madras.

events.title: Guruship of Guru Har Rai
events.summary: Community institutions and associations with Dara Shikoh amid changing Mughal relations.

events.title: Bombay marriage treaty provision
events.summary: Anglo-Portuguese agreement included Bombay in Catherine's dowry.

events.title: Guruship of Guru Har Krishan
events.summary: Child Guru remembered for service during illness; died of smallpox in 1664.

events.title: Charles II marries Catherine
events.summary: Distinguish wedding date from 1661 treaty and 1668 Company lease.

events.title: Dutch capture Cochin
events.summary: Portuguese lost an important Malabar base.

events.title: French East India Company established
events.summary: Colbert's initiative under Louis XIV.

events.title: Guruship of Guru Tegh Bahadur
events.summary: SGPC records recognition in 1664; travel and defence of religious conscience central to Sikh remembrance.

events.title: Bombay leased to English Company
events.summary: Crown transfer for annual rent of ten pounds.

events.title: French factory at Surat
events.summary: Caron developed an early French Indian trading post.

events.title: French factory at Masulipatnam
events.summary: Associated with Marcara.

events.title: French settlement at Pondicherry
events.summary: Initial occupation followed by Francois Martin's development of the settlement.

events.title: Guru Tegh Bahadur executed in Delhi
events.summary: Execution under Aurangzeb; Sis Ganj Sahib commemorates the site.

events.title: Guruship of Guru Gobind Singh
events.summary: Khalsa, collective discipline, and scriptural Guruship; last human Sikh Guru.

events.title: Charnock's Sutanuti settlement
events.summary: Important phase of Calcutta's growth, not purchase of all three villages that year.

events.title: Dutch headquarters shift to Nagapattinam
events.summary: Replaced Pulicat as principal Coromandel headquarters.

events.title: Dutch seize Pondicherry
events.summary: Demonstrates pre- and non-French European occupation.

events.title: Company acquires Calcutta village rights
events.summary: Zamindari rights over Sutanuti, Kalikata and Gobindapur.

events.title: Khalsa founded at Anandpur
events.summary: Guru Gobind Singh, Panj Pyare, khande-di-pahul and shared discipline.

events.title: Fort William and Bengal presidency develop
events.summary: Around 1700; institutional development rather than an exact single founding moment.

events.title: Guru Gobind Singh commissions Banda Bahadur
events.summary: Punjab mission entrusted to Banda Singh Bahadur; not an appointment by Guru Tegh Bahadur.

events.title: Guru Granth Sahib recognised as enduring Guru
events.summary: At the close of Guru Gobind Singh’s life at Nanded, personal succession gives way to enduring scriptural Guruship.

events.title: Surman embassy begins
events.summary: William Hamilton accompanied John Surman's mission to the Mughal court.

events.title: Farrukhsiyar's Company farmans
events.summary: Trading and rental privileges; Bengal annual payment of 3000 rupees. Private trade was not universally exempt.

events.title: Marathas capture Bassein and Salsette
events.summary: Reduced Portuguese northern possessions.

events.title: War of Austrian Succession
events.summary: European background to First Carnatic War.

events.title: Dupleix becomes governor
events.summary: French ambitions linked commerce to intervention in Indian politics.

events.title: Battle of Adyar or St Thome
events.summary: French force defeated Nawab Anwar-ud-din's force under Mahfuz Khan.

events.title: First Carnatic War
events.summary: English–French conflict in India connected to European war.

events.title: French capture Madras
events.summary: La Bourdonnais seized the English settlement.

events.title: Nizam-ul-Mulk dies
events.summary: Hyderabad succession dispute contributed to Second Carnatic War.

events.title: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle
events.summary: Madras restored to English; Louisbourg restored to France.

events.title: Battle of Ambur
events.summary: Anwar-ud-din killed; Muhammad Ali held out at Trichinopoly.

events.title: Second Carnatic War
events.summary: French and English intervention in Hyderabad and Carnatic succession struggles.

events.title: Nasir Jang killed
events.summary: Muzaffar Jang briefly succeeded, followed by Salabat Jang with French backing.

events.title: Clive's Arcot campaign
events.summary: Diversion reduced pressure on Muhammad Ali at Trichinopoly.

events.title: Battle of Kaveripak
events.summary: Part of the Arcot–Trichinopoly struggle in the Second Carnatic War.

events.title: Chanda Sahib killed
events.summary: A major French-supported claimant removed; English position strengthened.

events.title: Dupleix recalled and Pondicherry agreement
events.summary: Godeheu negotiated limits on political intervention.

events.title: Danish settlement at Serampore
events.summary: Frederiksnagore established in Bengal; source's 1676 date rejected.

events.title: Seven Years' War
events.summary: Global Anglo-French conflict connected to rivalry in India.

events.title: Siraj captures Fort William
events.summary: June capture; subsequent prisoner-death narrative disputed in numbers and detail.

events.title: Siraj-ud-Daulah succeeds Alivardi
events.summary: Disputes over privileges, fortifications and political authority sharpened.

events.title: Third Carnatic War
events.summary: Indian theatre of the Seven Years' War.

events.title: English recover Calcutta
events.summary: Clive and Admiral Watson retook the settlement early in the year.

events.title: Battle of Plassey
events.summary: Clive defeated Siraj through battle, conspiracy and defections; Mir Jafar installed; 24 Parganas gained.

events.title: Clive's first Bengal governorship
events.summary: Company influence and demands on the Nawab expanded after Plassey.

events.title: French siege of Madras fails
events.summary: Madras was not captured in this campaign.

events.title: Initial Company trade at Thatta
events.summary: Factory in Sindh opened in the Kalhora period, later abandoned.

events.title: Lally captures Fort St David
events.summary: French offensive in the Third Carnatic War.

events.title: Battle of Biderra
events.summary: English Company defeated Dutch forces near Chinsura; not immediate end of all Dutch settlements.

events.title: Battle of Wandiwash
events.summary: Eyre Coote defeated Lally; crucial Anglo-French turning point.

events.title: Mir Qasim replaces Mir Jafar
events.summary: Ceded Burdwan, Midnapore and Chittagong; pursued administrative and military independence.

events.title: Pondicherry falls to English
events.summary: French settlement captured during Third Carnatic War.

events.title: Third Battle of Panipat
events.summary: Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated Marathas, not Ibrahim Lodi.

events.title: Mir Qasim's customs conflict
events.summary: Abolition of internal duties challenged Company privilege; war and restoration of Mir Jafar followed.

events.title: Treaty of Paris
events.summary: French trading settlements restored subject to restrictions; territorial rivalry decisively curtailed.

events.title: Battle of Buxar
events.summary: Hector Munro defeated allied forces associated with Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah and Shah Alam II.

events.title: Allahabad settlement and imperial diwani
events.summary: Bengal, Bihar and Orissa revenue grant; emperor's annual payment 26 lakh; Awadh retained as buffer with indemnity.

events.title: Dual Government in Bengal
events.summary: Company held substantive power while Indian deputies and nominal Nawab bore administration; Clive's arrangement ended by Hastings.

events.title: Najm-ud-Daulah becomes Nawab
events.summary: Company control of finance, military power and appointments reduced effective independence.

events.title: Company–Hyderabad agreement
events.summary: Northern Circars and assistance arrangements formed background to First Mysore War.

events.title: First Anglo-Mysore War
events.summary: Hyder broke the opposing coalition and advanced towards Madras.

events.title: Tyagaraja’s lifetime
events.summary: Carnatic Trinity composer, mainly Telugu Rama devotion, Pancharatna Kritis.

events.title: Treaty of Madras
events.summary: Mutual restoration and defensive assistance against third-party attack.

events.title: Bengal famine
events.summary: Severe crop failure interacted with extraction and administrative failure; precise mortality estimates uncertain.

events.title: Maratha attack on Mysore
events.summary: British failure to assist Hyder deepened hostility after Treaty of Madras.

events.title: Dual Government abolished
events.summary: Warren Hastings ended the arrangement and reorganised Company revenue administration.

events.title: Madhav Rao I dies
events.summary: Peshwa succession dispute developed under Narayan Rao and Raghunath Rao.

events.title: Warren Hastings in Bengal
events.summary: Governorship followed by Governor-Generalship; ring-fence strategy associated with this period.

events.title: Narayan Rao murdered
events.summary: Raghunath Rao's claim challenged; Nana Phadnavis later supported infant Madhav Rao II.

events.title: Regulating Act
events.summary: Established Governor-General of Bengal and controls over presidency governments; Warren Hastings first held the office.

events.title: First Anglo-Maratha War
events.summary: Company intervention in Peshwa succession; Maratha resistance followed by Salbai settlement.

events.title: Treaty of Surat
events.summary: Bombay authorities supported Raghunath Rao in exchange for concessions.

events.title: Treaty of Purandar
events.summary: Upton's agreement recognised infant Peshwa and withdrew support to Raghunath Rao.

events.title: British capture Mahe
events.summary: French settlement under Hyder's protection became a trigger for renewed Mysore war.

events.title: Talegaon–Wadgaon campaign and convention
events.summary: Maratha forces compelled Bombay army's surrender; Hastings rejected the resulting convention.

events.title: Goddard captures Ahmedabad and Bassein
events.summary: Company counteroffensive in First Maratha War.

events.title: Pollilur and capture of Arcot
events.summary: Hyder defeated Baillie's force and took Arcot.

events.title: Popham captures Gwalior
events.summary: Assault on 3 August; source's 1781 date rejected.

events.title: Second Anglo-Mysore War
events.summary: Hyder and then Tipu fought the Company; concluded without decisive British territorial gains.

events.title: Battle of Porto Novo
events.summary: Eyre Coote defeated Hyder in the Second Mysore War.

events.title: Hyder Ali dies
events.summary: Tipu continued the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

events.title: Treaty of Salbai
events.summary: Madhav Rao II recognised, Raghunath Rao pensioned; Company retained Salsette; long peace with Marathas.

events.title: Treaty of Mangalore
events.summary: Mutual return of territories and prisoners concluded Second Mysore War.

events.title: Tipu's Ottoman diplomatic initiative
events.summary: Diplomatic mission to Ottoman Empire documented in archival research; the chapter's earlier range is not used.

events.title: William Jones on language affinities
events.summary: Comparative discussion of Sanskrit, Greek and Latin helped establish linguistic relationships. This contribution is distinct from proving any one specific Aryan homeland.

events.title: Tipu's French diplomatic initiative
events.summary: Envoys sought support as Mysore rebuilt its position.

events.title: Tipu attacks Travancore
events.summary: Conflict with British ally helped trigger Third Anglo-Mysore War.

events.title: Third Anglo-Mysore War
events.summary: Company allied with Nizam and Marathas; Cornwallis followed Medows in command.

events.title: Cornwallis captures Bangalore
events.summary: Advance followed by supply difficulties; renewed campaign led towards Seringapatam.

events.title: Treaty of Seringapatam
events.summary: Tipu lost half his dominions; 3.3 crore indemnity and two sons as hostages.

events.title: Hyderabad subsidiary arrangement
events.summary: Nizam accepted dependence and disbanded French corps.

events.title: Lord Wellesley's Governor-Generalship
events.summary: Systematic subsidiary dependence and major Mysore/Maratha expansion.

events.title: Tipu's revolutionary French contacts
events.summary: Contacts heightened Wellesley's suspicions but did not produce decisive French military assistance.

events.title: Tanjore administration transferred
events.summary: Treaty changed administrative control; not identical to every subsidiary agreement.

events.title: Seringapatam falls and Tipu dies
events.summary: 4 May: Harris commanded main army; reduced Wodeyar state restored under subsidiary dependence with Purnaiya as diwan.

events.title: Nana Phadnavis dies
events.summary: Loss of stabilising statesman preceded intensified Maratha rivalry.

events.title: Awadh territorial subsidiary settlement
events.summary: Wellesley's arrangement obtained territory to maintain Company forces.

events.title: Vithoji Holkar killed
events.summary: Peshwa's action deepened conflict with Yashwant Rao Holkar.

events.title: Holkar defeats Peshwa and Scindia at Poona
events.summary: Baji Rao II fled and sought British restoration.

events.title: Treaty of Bassein
events.summary: 31 December: Baji Rao II accepted subsidiary force, revenue cession and diplomatic restrictions.

events.title: Ahmednagar, Assaye and Argaon
events.summary: Arthur Wellesley's Deccan campaign against Scindia/Bhonsle.

events.title: Baji Rao II restored at Poona
events.summary: British forces implemented Bassein settlement.

events.title: Lake captures northern centres and wins Laswari
events.summary: Aligarh, Delhi and Agra; Mughal emperor came under British protection.

events.title: Second Anglo-Maratha War
events.summary: Company fought Scindia/Bhonsle and later Holkar; expansion exposed financial and military limits too.

events.title: Treaty of Deogaon
events.summary: Bhonsle ceded territory including Cuttack.

events.title: Treaty of Surji-Arjungaon
events.summary: Scindia accepted territorial losses and restrictions.

events.title: Holkar's continued resistance
events.summary: Campaigns and British failures at Bharatpur exposed limits of Company victory.

events.title: Treaty of Rajpurghat
events.summary: December peace with Holkar restored much territory; not a 1806 treaty.

events.title: Treaty of Tilsit and British strategic fears
events.summary: Franco-Russian cooperation increased concerns over routes towards India.

events.title: Company–Sindh friendship treaty
events.summary: Excluded French influence and offered territorial assurances; Minto's frontier diplomacy.

events.title: Pindari raids in Mirzapur and Shahabad
events.summary: Plundering bands posed challenges beyond their central Indian bases.

events.title: Pindari raids on Nizam's territories
events.summary: Added to pressure for a Company suppression campaign.

events.title: Nagpur subsidiary arrangement
events.summary: Appa Sahib accepted Company treaty before renewed resistance.

events.title: Pindari raids in Northern Circars
events.summary: British preparations for suppression intensified.

events.title: Battle of Kirkee
events.summary: November defeat of Peshwa's forces after attack on Poona Residency.

events.title: Battle of Sitabuldi
events.summary: November defeat of Appa Sahib's Nagpur forces.

events.title: Pindari suppression campaign
events.summary: Hastings' main campaign overlapped the Third Anglo-Maratha War; preparations began in 1816.

events.title: Third Anglo-Maratha War
events.summary: Peshwa, Nagpur and Holkar resistance defeated; Scindia constrained by a separate agreement.

events.title: Treaty of Gwalior
events.summary: Scindia accepted anti-Pindari cooperation and restrictions; stayed out of principal war.

events.title: Battle of Mahidpur
events.summary: 21 December: Holkar forces defeated at Mahidpur, not Baroda.

events.title: Peshwaship abolished and Satara created
events.summary: Baji Rao II pensioned at Bithur; Pratap Singh installed in dependent Satara state; Company paramountcy expanded.

events.title: Rajput protection arrangements
events.summary: States accepted British protection as Maratha dominance receded.

events.title: Treaty of Mandsaur
events.summary: Holkar accepted British dependence after Mahidpur.

events.title: Sindh treaty renewed
events.summary: Added exclusion of Americans and dealt with frontier issues.

events.title: First Anglo-Burmese War
events.summary: Historical war-date pair in revision; distinct from the Sikh wars.

events.title: Burnes explores Indus navigation
events.summary: Survey of commercial and strategic possibilities.

events.title: Company assumes Mysore administration
events.summary: Bentinck's government cited misgovernment; not annexation under lapse.

events.title: Ropar meeting
events.summary: Bentinck met Ranjit Singh on the Sutlej; frontier diplomacy and commercial cooperation.

events.title: Sindh navigation treaty
events.summary: Pottinger negotiated commercial access to the Indus.

events.title: Charter Act and Governor-General of India
events.summary: Bentinck became first Governor-General of India; distinct from Hastings' Bengal office.

events.title: Prinsep deciphers Brahmi inscriptions
events.summary: Key nineteenth-century decipherment; chapter’s 1887 date is rejected.

events.title: Sindh military and subsidiary dependence
events.summary: Residence, transit, military expenditure and unequal treaty demands expanded Company control.

events.title: Tripartite Treaty
events.summary: Company, Ranjit Singh and Shah Shuja connected to Afghan intervention.

events.title: First Anglo-Afghan War
events.summary: British intervention and reverses formed background to subsequent frontier expansion.

events.title: Ranjit Singh dies
events.summary: Sikh court succession struggles and army influence intensified.

events.title: Kharak Singh and Nau Nihal Singh die
events.summary: Deaths in contested circumstances destabilised Lahore succession.

events.title: Napier appointed in Sindh
events.summary: Political and military authority under Ellenborough preceded confrontation with Amirs.

events.title: Imamgarh destroyed
events.summary: Napier's action intensified conflict with Talpur Amirs.

events.title: Miani, Dubba and annexation of Sindh
events.summary: Napier defeated Talpur forces; Sindh annexed under Ellenborough.

events.title: Sher Singh assassinated; Duleep succeeds
events.summary: Child Maharaja under Rani Jindan's regency amid political turmoil.

events.title: Hira Singh killed
events.summary: Lahore power struggle continued; Jawahar Singh followed as wazir.

events.title: Battles of Mudki and Ferozeshah
events.summary: December battles with heavy fighting in the First Sikh War.

events.title: Danes sell Indian settlements
events.summary: Tranquebar and Serampore transferred to British.

events.title: First Anglo-Sikh War
events.summary: Hardinge Governor-General; Gough principal British commander.

events.title: Jawahar Singh killed
events.summary: Khalsa army influence and frontier mistrust intensified.

events.title: Battle of Aliwal
events.summary: January: Harry Smith defeated Sikh forces.

events.title: Battle of Baddowal
events.summary: January: Ranjodh Singh Majithia checked Harry Smith; Sikh success.

events.title: Battle of Sobraon
events.summary: February: Gough's decisive victory opened the way to Lahore.

events.title: Treaty of Amritsar
events.summary: March: Kashmir transferred to Gulab Singh for 75 lakh rupees.

events.title: Treaty of Bhairowal
events.summary: December: regency council under Resident; Jindan excluded; British control deepened.

events.title: Treaty of Lahore
events.summary: March: territorial cession, 1.5 crore indemnity, army reduction and British influence.

events.title: Battle of Ramnagar
events.summary: November fighting met strong Sikh resistance.

events.title: Dalhousie's Governor-Generalship
events.summary: Annexation by war, lapse and alleged misgovernment; distinct pretexts must be separated.

events.title: Satara annexed under lapse
events.summary: Refusal of adopted heir's political succession.

events.title: Second Anglo-Sikh War
events.summary: Multan uprising and broader resistance led to annexation.

events.title: Battle of Chillianwala
events.summary: January battle inflicted heavy losses on British forces.

events.title: Battle of Gujrat
events.summary: February: Gough's decisive victory in Second Sikh War.

events.title: Jaitpur and Sambalpur annexed
events.summary: Lapse cases distinct from Awadh's alleged misgovernment.

events.title: Punjab Board of Administration formed
events.summary: Henry Lawrence, John Lawrence and Charles Mansel.

events.title: Punjab annexed
events.summary: 29 March under Dalhousie; Duleep pensioned; not lapse.

events.title: Punjab Chief Commissionership
events.summary: Board abolished; John Lawrence appointed Chief Commissioner.

events.title: Duleep Singh goes to Britain
events.summary: Later exile, not simultaneous removal with Jindan in 1849.

events.title: Jhansi and Nagpur annexed
events.summary: Rulers' deaths and succession disputes preceded final annexation; lapse applied.

events.title: Awadh annexed
events.summary: Wajid Ali Shah deposed on alleged misgovernment; not Doctrine of Lapse.

events.title: Revolt against Company rule
events.summary: Annexations, military disruption and political grievances formed part of its background.

events.title: Punjab Lieutenant-Governorship begins
events.summary: John Lawrence briefly held the first Lieutenant-Governorship from January 1859; Robert Montgomery succeeded him in February.

events.title: Foote discovers Pallavaram handaxe
events.summary: Robert Bruce Foote’s discovery is a landmark in the study of Indian prehistory.

events.title: Carlleyle documents Indian rock paintings
events.summary: Early modern discovery/documentation, not the date the paintings were made.

events.title: Mysore administration restored
events.summary: Rendition under Ripon; Wodeyar ruler resumed administration under paramountcy.

events.title: Arthashastra brought to modern scholarly attention
events.summary: R. Shamasastry’s identification/initial scholarly announcement; publication followed.

events.title: Sahni excavates Harappa
events.summary: Daya Ram Sahni’s excavations initiate recognition of the major urban site.

events.title: Banerji investigates Mohenjo-daro
events.summary: R.D. Banerji’s work helps reveal the second great urban site.

events.title: Indus civilisation publicly announced
events.summary: John Marshall announces the recognition of a previously unknown ancient civilisation; distinguish discovery, excavation and publication.

events.title: Majumdar excavates Amri
events.summary: Early regional occupation and later cultural sequences documented.

events.title: Majumdar investigates Chanhudaro
events.summary: Subsequent Mackay excavations reveal specialised craft activity.

events.title: Y.D. Sharma begins Ropar excavations
events.summary: Multi-period settlement and cemetery evidence; the site is on the Sutlej.

events.title: F.A. Khan excavates Kot Diji
events.summary: Early Harappan fortified settlement and destruction layers documented.

events.title: Lothal excavations
events.summary: S.R. Rao’s excavations identify the basin/dockyard interpretation, workshops and other urban features.

events.title: Wakankar identifies Bhimbetka shelters
events.summary: V.S. Wakankar’s survey brought the rock shelters to scholarly attention.

events.title: Alamgirpur excavated
events.summary: Y.D. Sharma investigates Late Harappan remains in the Hindon region.

events.title: Kalibangan major excavation programme
events.summary: B.B. Lal, B.K. Thapar and colleagues investigate early/mature phases, ploughed field and features interpreted as fire altars.

events.title: Portuguese rule ends in Goa, Daman and Diu
events.summary: Indian military action ended the remaining Portuguese enclaves in these territories.

events.title: Surkotada identified
events.summary: J.P. Joshi identifies the Kutch site; equid remains later prompt a disputed horse identification.

events.title: Banawali excavations begin
events.summary: R.S. Bisht’s work documents early/mature settlement and the terracotta plough model.

events.title: Dholavira major excavations
events.summary: R.S. Bisht’s programme exposes fortified divisions, water management and the ten-sign inscription; field seasons are often described as 1989/90–2005.

events.title: Sanchi inscribed as World Heritage
events.summary: Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi entered the UNESCO World Heritage List; the site contains many building phases, not only an Ashokan monument.

events.title: Rigveda manuscripts enter UNESCO Memory of the World
events.summary: Registration of Rigveda manuscripts preserved at Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, Pune: documentary heritage recognition, not designation as a World Heritage Site.

events.title: Bhirrana chronology and climate study
events.summary: Research proposes earlier local occupation and examines monsoon/subsistence change; this does not redate the mature urban phase to 7000 BCE.

events.title: Attirampakkam Middle Palaeolithic dating published
events.summary: Luminescence study dates the local transition around 385 ±64 ka and continuation to 172 ±41 ka; not a uniform subcontinental chronology.

events.title: Rakhigarhi genome study published
events.summary: One successfully analysed Harappan genome shows no detected Steppe-pastoralist ancestry in that individual; broad genetic/linguistic claims require more evidence.

events.title: Five iconic archaeological destinations proposed
events.summary: Budget 2020–21 includes Rakhigarhi, Dholavira, Hastinapur, Sivasagar and Adichanallur; proposal is distinct from completion.

events.title: Dholavira inscribed as World Heritage
events.summary: UNESCO recognises the Harappan city; its urban layout and water management are key attributes.

events.title: Mehrgarh Period I re-dating study
events.summary: Human tooth-enamel radiocarbon results propose c.5250–4650 cal BCE, challenging conventional much earlier dates; broader regional conclusions require further evidence.
